newsitem.title: USA: Iomega drive bootable, shares rise.
newsitem.headline: Iomega drive bootable, shares rise.

text.p: Shares of Iomega Corp rose on Friday after the company released news its internal Zip drives will be fully bootable.

"There's a checklist of things Iomega must do to put themselves in a position to truly replace the floppy disk. This is one of them," said Joe Besecker of Emerald Research in Lancaster, Pa. He said the bootable news will widen Zipss appeal, adding that shares rose on the news.
Iomega shares were up 1/4 at 18-1/4 after reaching as high as 19-7/8. More than 16.5 million shares changed hands.

On Thursday, the Roy, Utah-based company said its internal Zip drives for original equipment manufacturers (OEM) are expected to be fully bootable, increasing the drive's functionality and flexibility and enhance its ability to become the new removable storage standard replacing the 1.44MB floppy.

Iomega's strategy has been two-fold, Besecker said. It has gone after both the OEM market and retail business. "They've consumerized technology," he said. By being popular with consumers, Iomega creates interest and demand on the part of big equipment manufacturers.

Shares of IMP Inc were also higher on spillover support because the company is a supplier to Iomega. But Besecker noted Iomega now uses other suppliers also. "They're (IMP) not as significant as they were," he said.
